question: A 22-year-old woman with confirmed IDA (Hb 8.5 g/dL) is started on oral ferrous sulphate. What is the expected haemoglobin response after 4 weeks of adequate therapy, and for how long should iron be continued AFTER haemoglobin normalises?

answers.text: Hb rises by 0.5 g/dL; continue for 2 weeks after normalisation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A rise of only 0.5 g/dL suggests inadequate response — check compliance, absorption (tea/antacids reduce absorption), ongoing blood loss, or wrong diagnosis. Two weeks post-normalisation is insufficient to replenish iron stores.

answers.text: Hb rises by ~1–2 g/dL; continue for 3 months after normalisation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. With adequate oral iron therapy, haemoglobin typically rises by 1–2 g/dL every 3–4 weeks. Treatment must continue for 3 months (approximately 100 days) after normalisation to fully replenish iron stores (serum ferritin target > 50 µg/L).

answers.text: Hb rises by ~1–2 g/dL; stop immediately when Hb reaches 12 g/dL

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Stopping at Hb normalisation is a common mistake. Iron stores (ferritin) take an additional 3 months to replenish. Early discontinuation leads to relapse of IDA within weeks to months.

A rise of 3–4 g/dL in 4 weeks is faster than expected for oral iron. Indefinite continuation is not recommended once stores are replenished. If stores cannot be maintained, investigate ongoing causes (menorrhagia, GI bleed) rather than perpetual supplementation.

overallFeedback.feedback: Key IDA treatment rule: Hb rises ~1–2 g/dL per 4 weeks. Continue oral iron for 3 months AFTER Hb normalises to replenish ferritin stores (target ferritin > 50 µg/L). Stopping at Hb normalisation guarantees early relapse.
Correct. The rule of 1–2 g/dL rise per month and 3 months post-normalisation for store repletion is essential knowledge for IDA management.
